description: Lookups by bucket (PROTOCOL §19.9) for the key-transparency log and the handle log, and the handle log itself (§21.5). A bucket is every label whose first `bits` bits are `prefix` (⌈bits/4⌉ hex digits, unused low bits zero); its answer carries the head, the leaves in label order and the map siblings from depth bits-1 up to 0. A reader recomputes the depth-`bits` subtree from the leaves with the map leaf hash and the empty subtrees of §19.2, folds it up through the siblings by the prefix's bits, and compares it with the head's mapRoot after verifying the head under the pinned key in the log's own context. Handle-log leaves also carry the record (value), ts (a whole hour), the owner's sig and the audit path of the entry at index, which verifies the handle leaf under logRoot. Every response_json is a response as served; every must_refuse must fail. The handle labels are stand-ins (the log never computes a label); owner_rule_refusals are publishes the log refuses, with the status and code it answers.

must_refuse.why: a label left out of the bucket
a label added to the bucket
a version that is not the map's
two leaves out of label order
the answer for the other half, presented as this one
a head the log key signed in the HANDLE log's context
the record changed (pow 28 → 16): it is not the entry the log tree holds at its index
a ts that is not a whole hour
an older record of the label (version 2) in place of the latest
a head the handle log key signed in the KEY-TRANSPARENCY context

owner_rule_refusals.why: a claim on a held label
an update naming the stranger as owner
an update naming the owner, signed by the stranger
an update changing the recovery commitment
an update by the owner the recover replaced
a recover with the spent recovery key
a recover signed by the old owner for the new
a version that does not exceed the label's
a record that is not its canonical encoding (a space)
an introduction key without its X25519 key (intro set, xintro null)
